c.st: DewDrop – A Formal Language for Social Networks
c.x:
> a high level of social control is customary and desired.

a high level of social control is customary because i live in the world as it is now. but that is NOT the world i desire to live in.

the way things work now, social control is implicit and heavily enforced. by making it explicit, you can reduce the extent to which it's enforced - and by speaking in formal languages, you can show that anyone who makes a claim gets credit for being right, regardless of their station in life or how big their audience is.

c.st: AGI is an engineering problem, not a model training problem
c.x: This bogus argument has been refuted numerous times--read Dennett's book "Freedom Evolves" for one sort of response. And whether people are "pretending" something is irrelevant (and ad hominem, and not even true). The plain fact remains that all evidence and logic supports physicalism, and even if you entertain dualistic ideas like those of David Chalmers they don't give you free will, they don't counter determinism.

c.st: Ask HN:  How can you be rational and still believe in free will?
c.x:
'Freedom evolves' by Daniel Dennett deals with this.
http://www.amazon.com/Freedom-Evolves-Daniel-C-Dennett/dp/0142003840/

Our future may be fixed, but our nature is not. We don't have a 'God's eye view' that sees all our past and future laid out before us. From our perspectives conditions change and we change to adapt to them to the extent possible.

It seems to me the confusion mainly arises if you consider your mind as being not subject to nature's laws...

c.st: Ask HN:  How can you be rational and still believe in free will?

You might not agree with his conclusions, as they're fairly radical, but it answers the question of the original post.
